item.title: #3583045: tool:info --format=json prints [] instead of {} for a tool with no inputs or outputs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583045 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

The tool:info --format=json Drush command in the Tool module now always prints inputs, outputs, and output_schema as JSON objects ({}), even when a tool declares none. Previously an empty PHP array serialized to a JSON list ([]) in that case, which broke consumers that expect a map keyed by name, including typed decoders that reject a list where an object is required.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ToolInfoCommand::outputInfoAsJson() built $data['inputs'] and $data['outputs'] directly as PHP arrays populated in a loop over the tool's definitions. When a tool had no input or output definitions, the array stayed empty, and PHP's Json::encode() (like native json_encode()) renders an empty array as [] rather than {} since there is no key information to distinguish a list from a map. The fix builds $inputs and $outputs as local arrays as before, then assigns $data['inputs'] = $inputs ?: new \ArrayObject() (and likewise for outputs and output_schema), so Json::encode() serializes the empty case as an object. The test ToolInfoCommandTest::testToolInfoSimpleTool() was extended to assert "inputs":{}, "outputs":{}, and "output_schema":{} for a tool with no requirements.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3582967: Harden the 'administer tool' permission
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3582967 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

The Tool Explorer's administer tool permission, which controls execution of arbitrary Tool plugins (including entity creation, modification, and deletion), previously had only a bare title with no warning that it was a sensitive, security-relevant permission. It is now flagged as restricted in Drupal's permissions UI, and its description explicitly warns that granting it allows executing tools that can change site data and configuration. A new view tool information permission lets roles browse the list of registered tools and view their input, output, and configuration schemas without being able to run them, so site builders no longer have to grant full execute access just to let someone audit what tools exist.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Permission change: The administer tool permission is now marked restrict access: true with a warning description; a new view tool information permission grants read-only browsing of Tool Explorer definitions without allowing execution.

Technical details

The fix in tool.permissions.yml adds restrict access: true and a warning description to administer tool, and introduces a second permission, view tool information (also restricted), covering read-only browsing. tool_explorer.routing.yml changes the tool_explorer.list and tool_explorer.view routes' _permission requirement to 'view tool information+administer tool' (either permission grants access), while tool_explorer.execute keeps requiring administer tool alone.

ToolExplorerController::listTools() now builds the row operations conditionally: the view link is always present, but the execute dropbutton link is only added when $this->currentUser()->hasPermission('administer tool') is true. Because the rendered operations now vary by permission, the list render array's #cache was given a user.permissions cache context to avoid serving a cached row with the Execute link to a user who lacks administer tool. A new kernel test, ToolExplorerAccessTest, asserts both permissions are marked restricted, checks route access for anonymous, no-permission, read-only, and administrator accounts, and verifies which operations links appear per role.

Upgrade

Sites that grant administer tool to a role only so users can browse the Tool Explorer without executing tools should switch that role to the new view tool information permission instead:

view tool information:
  title: 'View tool information'
  description: 'Browse tool definitions in Tool Explorer, including input, output, and configuration schemas.'
  restrict access: true

Custom code checking access to the Explorer's list or view routes should account for the new _permission: 'view tool information+administer tool' requirement (either permission suffices), while the execute route still requires administer tool alone.

item.title: #3583060: Structure-reading constraints on a map input throw instead of validating
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583060 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

The Tool module (a contributed module that lets developers define typed, self-contained "tools" callable from Drush, controllers, ECA, AI agents, or MCP servers) had a bug in input validation: a map input (MapInputDefinition) whose author declared a structure-reading constraint, such as Symfony's ComplexData naming one of the map's own declared properties, would crash with an uncaught InvalidArgumentException: Property X is unknown. instead of reporting a normal validation violation. This is now fixed so such constraints validate correctly and report per-property violations as expected. No in-tree or known consumer tool currently declares this kind of constraint, so the practical exposure before this fix was limited to third-party tool authors who did.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

This was the second regression in the same code path. #3583004 split map validation out of core's Context::validate() into a per-property walk, which silently skipped map-level declared constraints (the map counterpart of the list regression fixed in #3583048). #3583028 then restored enforcement of declared constraints, but rebuilt the typed data from a bare createDataDefinition($definition->getDataType()), a map with no properties, so any constraint that reads the map's structure (like ComplexData naming sku) found the property "unknown" and threw outside any catch.

The fix, in TypedInputsTrait::validateDeclaredConstraints(), builds the typed data for a MapDataDefinition from EffectiveDataDefinition::createFrom($definition) instead, which carries the map's declared properties, while a bare data type is still used for lists (no list-level constraint reads items). Each declared constraint is now run individually through RecursiveValidator::startContext() as a non-root call rather than delegating to a single recursive validate(), so a constraint only visits the members it actually names instead of re-validating every property or descending into entity fields. A new $members_rejected flag lets exceptions from a constraint reading a property whose value already failed its own type check be swallowed (the value is already rejected), while exceptions from genuinely misdeclared constraints, such as ComplexData naming a property the map does not declare, still throw loudly, consistent with the authoring-mistake ruling from #3583048. The regression lineage and the interaction with the earlier required-empty-collection fix (#3583040) and the entity-input change (#3583028) are documented in the updated method docblock.

item.title: #3583035: tool:run sends the PHP output values, not the formatted result
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583035 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

The tool:run Drush command (used to invoke and inspect Tool module plugins from the command line) was sending raw PHP values instead of the values formatted according to each output's advertised schema. This meant, for example, that a timestamp output showed up as a raw Unix integer (1785606907) instead of the documented date-time string, and an empty map printed its internal \ArrayObject class name instead of {}. The MCP bridge already did this correctly; tool:run was the last in-tree caller reading unformatted values. The command now sends the same formatted output that other invokers, like the MCP bridge, produce.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ToolRunCommand now emits the formatted output values (matching each output's advertised schema) instead of the tool's raw PHP values; an empty map now serializes as {} instead of an \ArrayObject class name.

Technical details

ToolRunCommand::runTool() previously called $tool->getOutputValues() (guarded by a success check, since output contexts are unset on failure and getOutputValues() throws otherwise) to build the outputs array. It now calls $tool->getFormattedResult()->getContextValues() unconditionally: a failed tool simply carries no output values, so the success guard is removed. getFormattedResult() applies the transform pipeline added in the related timestamp/decimal/datetime coercion work (#3583030), turning entities into handles and spelling timestamps, decimals, and dates the way the schema's date-time etc. types describe.

ToolOutputTrait::formatValue() and ToolRunCommand::serializeOutputs() were both updated to special-case \ArrayObject (used to represent an empty map) so it serializes as {} in both the JSON and human-readable text output paths, rather than falling through to is_object() handling that printed the class name.

Docblocks were added to TypedOutputsInterface::getOutputValue() and getOutputValues() clarifying that these return the tool's raw PHP values (for the tool itself and its tests), and that anything leaving the process should read getFormattedResult() instead. The issue also raised whether to rename these to something like getRawOutputValues()/getFormattedOutputValues() to make the distinction harder to get wrong, but that rename was deferred as a pre-1.0 API decision; only the docblock clarification landed here.

Upgrade

If code or scripts invoke drush tool:run --json and parse specific output fields, expect formatted values rather than raw PHP values, for example:

# Before: raw Unix timestamp
"date": 1785606907

# After: formatted per the output's date-time schema
"date": "2026-08-01T17:55:07+00:00"

Empty map outputs now serialize as {} instead of an ArrayObject class name string.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 21, 2026

  • csakiistvan (1xINTERNET)
  • mglaman (Acquia)
  • dries

item.title: #3583030: outputSchema describes a timestamp member as date-time, structuredContent sends integer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583030 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

The Tool module builds an MCP outputSchema for each tool's declared output types, but the actual structuredContent payload it sent for a tool's result didn't always match that schema. A timestamp output, for example, was advertised as an RFC 3339 date-time string but sent as a raw Unix integer. Since the MCP spec requires servers to send structured results that conform to the schema, and expects clients to validate against it, this mismatch could make an otherwise-correct tool result get rejected by a compliant client. The fix converts affected values to the format the schema promises before they go out over the wire.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: getFormattedResult() now converts timestamp, decimal, and DateTime-constrained datetime_iso8601 output values, plus empty map outputs, to match the wire format their advertised outputSchema describes (e.g. a Unix timestamp becomes an RFC 3339 string, an empty map becomes {} instead of []); getResult()/getOutputValue() keep returning the original PHP values.

Technical details

The conversion lives in a new OutputTypeCoercionSubscriber, an event subscriber on ToolOutputTransformEvent that runs after invoker-specific subscribers but before the recursive subscriber that walks list/map items, so nested members get the same treatment. It handles four mismatches: a timestamp value is reformatted from a Unix integer to DateTimeInterface::RFC3339 when the active core is 11.1+ (core's schema-aware TimestampNormalizer describes it as a date-time string there; older cores use the module's LegacyTypedDataNormalizer, which describes it as an integer, so it's left alone); a decimal int or float is formatted as a fixed-point string via a new shared DecimalStringTrait (extracted from InputTypeCoercionSubscriber, which already needed the same logic for input coercion); a datetime_iso8601 value carrying the DateTime constraint is reformatted from the offset-less storage spelling (Y-m-d\TH:i:s) to RFC 3339, but only when it matches that exact storage format, anything with an offset or otherwise non-conforming is left untouched; and an empty PHP array for a non-multiple map output is replaced with new \ArrayObject() so it JSON-encodes as {} instead of [].

The new AdvertisedOutputSchemaConformanceTest exercises every discovered tool with schema-conforming sample inputs and validates each formatted output against its normalized schema, plus pins the exact converted spellings so a value that happens to validate but changes meaning (a shifted timezone, a rounded decimal) is still caught.

item.title: #3583040: A required list rejects the empty array its JSON Schema allows
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583040 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

Tool API's validation for required list inputs and outputs previously disagreed with the JSON Schema it publishes. A required list (for example, search results, validation problems, or changed IDs) is advertised in the schema as accepting an empty array, but validation rejected [] with "This value should not be null." This meant a tool could return a valid empty result and still fail its own output validation, or a client following the published schema could send a value the tool would reject anyway. Validation now matches the schema: a required list accepts [], and only NULL (a genuinely missing value) is rejected. Required maps are unaffected: an empty object still fails validation as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: A required list input or output (OutputDefinition/InputDefinition with multiple: TRUE, or ListInputDefinition/ListOutputDefinition) now validates successfully when set to an empty array []; only NULL is rejected. Required maps are unchanged and still reject an empty value.

Technical details

The root cause is core's NotNullConstraintValidator, which Tool API inherits as a default constraint whenever a definition is marked required. That validator treats any empty ListInterface or ComplexDataInterface as NULL before checking for nullness, so an empty list tripped the same rejection as a genuinely missing value, even though typed data's "not empty" reading of required diverges from JSON Schema's "key is present" reading.

The fix is in EffectiveDataDefinition: when building the effective typed data definition for validation, a list definition (anything implementing ListDataDefinitionInterface) is no longer marked required, which keeps core's NotNull off of it entirely. TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValue() and TypedOutputsTrait::validateOutputValue() each detect the case that NotNull would otherwise have caught (a NULL value against a required list definition) and explicitly run a NotNull check via the new ValueViolationsTrait::validateListNotNull(), so a NULL list is still rejected with the same message as before. Maps keep their required flag unchanged: they're objects with named properties rather than sequences, and core already skips validating the properties of an empty map (drupal/drupal#3256536), so an empty required map still fails.

A tool that needs at least one item still declares that explicitly with a Count constraint, which the normalizer publishes as minItems in the JSON Schema, for example constraints: ['Count' => ['min' => 1]].</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">If a tool relies on a required list rejecting an empty value, add an explicit Count constraint rather than depending on the removed implicit behavior:

new InputDefinition('entity:node', 'Nodes', 'The nodes to export.', required: TRUE, multiple: TRUE, constraints: ['Count' => ['min' => 1]]);
// {"type": "array", "minItems": 1, ...}

No changes are needed for tools that already treat an empty required list as valid, or for required maps, whose validation is unchanged.

Contribution

  • Opened: September 23, 2026

item.title: #3585917: Tool call responses are silently dropped when the handler renders anything (fiber suspension misread as scheduling protocol)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585917 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

In the MCP Server module, a tools/call (and prompts/get, resources/read, completion/complete) request whose handler rendered markup or loaded an entity could complete its work successfully but never send a response back to the client. The client would see nothing, and could wrongly retry the call (creating a duplicate) or assume the operation had failed when it had actually succeeded. This is now fixed: any handler that triggers Drupal's own internal suspension mechanics (rendering, entity loading, theme registry lookups) returns its result normally instead of silently dropping it.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The MCP PHP SDK dispatches each request inside a PHP Fiber and interprets any Fiber::suspend() call from within the handler as a ClientGateway operation addressed back to the client (for example, a sampling request). Drupal 10.3+'s own internals use the same mechanism for unrelated purposes: the renderer and EntityStorageBase::loadMultiple() suspend with FiberResumeType::Immediate while resolving placeholders, and the theme registry suspends with no payload on a cold cache. When a tool handler triggered one of these, the SDK misread it as its own scheduling protocol, logged Fiber yielded unexpected payload, and answered the request as text/event-stream instead of application/json, so a JSON-only client never saw the result.

The fix adds Drupal\mcp_server\Capability\FiberShield, which runs the handler in its own inner fiber. It inspects each suspended payload: if it's an array with a type key (a genuine ClientGateway operation), it's re-yielded up to the SDK and the reply is passed back down; anything else (Drupal's internal suspends) is resumed immediately in place, exactly as Drupal's synchronous render path already does. ShieldedReferenceHandler wraps the SDK's ReferenceHandler to cover tools/call, prompts/get, and resources/read, which all flow through it, and ShieldedCompletionProvider wraps each argument-completion provider individually because completion/complete is dispatched directly by the SDK rather than through the reference handler. McpServerFactory wires both decorators in. The issue notes upstream declined to fix this in the SDK itself (php-sdk#505), so the module shields its own dispatch paths instead.

item.title: #3583028: Accept integer map keys and any entity as an entity input
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583028 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

The Tool module (a contributed module providing a plugin type for defining typed, self-contained "tools" callable from Drush, controllers, ECA, AI agents, or MCP servers) had two gaps in how it validated the values passed into a tool's inputs. First, an input declared as entity:user_role (or any config entity type) rejected valid Role or NodeType objects, because the check only accepted content entities even though core derives an entity:TYPE data type for config entities too. Second, the entity type and bundle a tool author declared were not actually checked, so a Node passed where an entity:user was expected would pass validation and only fail later, deep inside the tool's own code, with a confusing error. Separately, a config mapping such as system.site's page.403/page.404 keys, which PHP stores as integers, crashed input-definition building entirely. All three cases are fixed: any entity type now satisfies its matching entity:TYPE input, mismatched types or bundles are reported as a proper validation violation naming the input, and integer-keyed mappings work.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValue() now checks an entity input's declared entity type and bundle (and any author-declared constraints) instead of only checking that a value is a ContentEntityInterface; a mismatched entity now produces a validation violation naming the input instead of failing later inside the tool. MapDefinitionBase::setPropertyDefinitions() now accepts integer property names.

Technical details

The entity branch of TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValue() (mirrored in TypedOutputsTrait) used to require $typed_data->getValue() instanceof ContentEntityInterface. It now accepts any EntityInterface, and when the value is an entity, builds a constraint set from the effective definition's dynamic EntityType/Bundle constraints merged with any constraints the input author declared, then runs only those against the entity via the typed data validator, explicitly excluding full entity/field validation and the entity type's own constraints (like EntityChanged). This required generalizing what was validateListConstraints() (list-only) into validateDeclaredConstraints(), used for both lists and maps, since a Count constraint on a map now binds the map's property count rather than being invalid on a scalar. That in turn made Count on a MapInputDefinition surface as minProperties/maxProperties in the generated JSON Schema, via a new ContextDefinitionNormalizer::applyMapConstraintSchema().

MapDefinitionBase::setPropertyDefinitions() now accepts is_int($name) alongside is_string($name), since PHP casts numeric array keys like 403 to integers. Several callers that pass property names into typed parameters (RecursiveToolValueTransformSubscriber, ContextDefinitionNormalizer, MapDefinitionNormalizer, MapAdapter) were updated to cast the key to (string) where a string-typed argument is expected.

item.title: #3583012: Ship a use-drupal-tools agent skill so agents discover, inspect, and run Tool operations
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583012 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

Tool now ships a ready-made Agent Skill file that teaches AI coding agents how to find, inspect, and run its operations. Previously, every module that consumes Tool and ships its own Agent Skill (like canvas_tools) had to restate the same mechanics: how to search for an operation, read its input contract, and call it via drush tool:run. Those hand-written explanations drift whenever an input is renamed. With this skill in place, agents load a single, maintained procedure straight from the module, and downstream modules can shrink their own skills to their domain-specific steps while pointing back at this one for the underlying Tool mechanics.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Module now ships .agents/skills/use-drupal-tools/SKILL.md, a procedural Agent Skill (per the Agent Skills specification) documenting the tool:search, tool:list, tool:info, and tool:run Drush commands for AI coding agents.

Technical details

The change adds .agents/skills/use-drupal-tools/SKILL.md, following the Agent Skills specification (a SKILL.md with frontmatter name/description that an agent loads on demand). It documents the four-step workflow: search or list operations with tool:search/tool:list --format=json and filter by operation kind (read/explain/transform are non-mutating, write/trigger are); inspect an operation's input_schema/inputs/output_schema with tool:info --format=json rather than copying inputs from an example; run it with tool:run --input=... --json and branch on the {success, message, outputs}/{success, error, error_type} shape; and always pass --uid so checkAccess() runs as the real caller instead of anonymous or uid 1. It also documents that the same plugin id is exposed as an MCP tool name via mcp_server_tool_bridge (mcp_tool_config entities) and as a function name in tool_ai_connector, and lists several open bugs agents need to work around (e.g. silent dropping of malformed --input, exit code 0 on not-found lookups, and access denials that don't surface a reason).

Alongside the skill file, docs/usage/agent-skills.md and a README.md section explain how the skill reaches a project: drupal/ai_best_practices syncs .agents/skills/ from installed modules into the project root on composer install, or it can be copied/symlinked manually. The commit also formalizes an existing create-tool-plugins skill (scaffolding a #[Tool] plugin) alongside the new one and adds both to the mkdocs.yml navigation.

item.title: #3583048: Constraints declared on a ListInputDefinition are never validated
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583048 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

In the Tool module, constraints declared directly on a ListInputDefinition (such as a minimum or maximum item count via Count) were silently ignored during validation. Only constraints on the list's item definition were checked, so a list required to have at least two elements would happily accept one, or even zero. This was a regression introduced by an earlier refactor (#3583004) that moved the call validating a value's own constraints into an else branch meant for maps, which accidentally excluded lists from ever reaching it. The fix restores enforcement of list-level constraints so validation matches what the module's generated JSON Schema already advertised (minItems, maxItems, etc.).

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The regression lived in TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValue(): the list branch iterated items and validated each one, but never validated the list value itself against its own declared constraints, because the fall-through to typed-data validation had been moved into the map-only else branch.

Simply restoring the fall-through was rejected because it would also run typed-data's implicit NotNull default constraint, which treats an empty list as "missing" and rejects it with "This value should not be null", a false positive not implied by the advertised schema (see #3583040). Instead, the fix adds a new validateListConstraints() method that reads only the constraints the author explicitly declared via getConstraints(), builds them through the validation constraint manager, and validates the list's typed-data representation against just that constraint set, bypassing the implicit typed-data defaults entirely. It also calls the existing resetTypedDataPrototypes() helper before building the list, to avoid an unrelated prototype-poisoning issue with lists of any-typed items (#3616328). Item-level violations continue to be collected separately via addItemViolations(), so failures are not double-reported. Output validation (validateOutputs()) was already unaffected since it uses full typed-data validation directly.

item.title: #3583019: Remove ContextDefinitionInterface from the definition interfaces
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583019 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

The tool module's InputDefinitionInterface and OutputDefinitionInterface no longer extend Drupal core's ContextDefinitionInterface. This completes a three-step plan (after #3583016 and #3583017) to detach the module's input and output definitions from core's Plugin Context system now that they are built on typed data instead. Code that relied on tool definitions also behaving like core context definitions (type hints, instanceof checks against ContextDefinitionInterface, or event subscribers written against it) will stop matching. The module also removes the deprecated getInput()/getOutput() (and getInputs()/getOutputs()) accessors that minted Context objects on demand, and the deprecated MapContextDefinition/ListContextDefinition classes. None of this affects how tools are declared, the value APIs, or the JSON Schema the module publishes; the ai module integration is unaffected because tool_ai_connector already converts between tool definitions and core context definitions at that boundary.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: InputDefinitionInterface and OutputDefinitionInterface no longer extend ContextDefinitionInterface; getDataDefinition() and isSatisfiedBy() are removed from those definitions, TypedInputsInterface::getInput()/getInputs() and TypedOutputsInterface::getOutput()/getOutputs() are removed, and MapContextDefinition/ListContextDefinition are deleted.

Technical details

The bridge trait that let tool definitions answer as ContextDefinitionInterface (ContextDefinitionBridgeTrait, added in #3583017) is deleted and replaced by a smaller ToolDataDefinitionTrait that only carries the value semantics the definitions still need: isMultiple()/setMultiple() and getDefaultValue()/setDefaultValue(), now declared directly on InputDefinitionInterface and OutputDefinitionInterface rather than inherited from core's context interface. The bridge methods that existed purely to satisfy ContextDefinitionInterface, getDataDefinition() and isSatisfiedBy(), are gone; callers that previously called $definition->getDataDefinition() to get a typed data definition (for example ConfigureToolPluginForm and ExecuteToolPluginForm) now call EffectiveDataDefinition::createFrom($definition) instead.

TypedInputsInterface::getInput()/getInputs() and TypedOutputsInterface::getOutput()/getOutputs(), deprecated since tool:1.0.0-beta10, are removed along with their on-demand Context minting; TypedInputsTrait and TypedOutputsTrait are deleted entirely. The deprecated MapContextDefinition and ListContextDefinition classes, thin wrappers around MapDefinitionBase/ListDefinitionBase for constructing core-style context definitions, are also deleted. The acceptance shim that still lets a plugin declare an output using a core ContextDefinition/EntityContextDefinition remains for now; its removal is tracked separately in #3583050.

Upgrade

Replace any use of the removed context accessors with the typed-data equivalents:

// Before:
$context = $plugin->getInput('name');
$plugin->setInput('name', $context);
$output_context = $plugin->getOutput('name');

// After:
$value = $plugin->getInputValue('name');
// or, for the typed data object:
$data = $plugin->getInputData('name');
$plugin->setInputValue('name', $value);

item.title: #3583018: Store input and output values as typed data instead of Context objects
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583018 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

The Tool API module (part of the AI tooling ecosystem) changes how it stores the values passed into and out of a tool. Previously every input and output value was wrapped in a core Context object; now values are stored as typed data directly. For developers this mostly matters through new accessor methods: getInputData() and getOutputData() return the value as typed data, while the existing getInput(), getOutput(), getInputs(), getOutputs() and setInput() methods are deprecated (they still work, minting a Context object on demand) and will be removed in tool:1.0.0-rc1. Sites and modules using only getInputValue()/setInputValue()/getOutputValue()/setOutputValue() are unaffected. The module's integration with the ai module's function-call contract, which still requires core context definitions, keeps working through a new adaptation layer in tool_ai_connector.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: InputDefinitionInterface and OutputDefinitionInterface now also extend DataDefinitionInterface (not just ContextDefinitionInterface), and both formally declare isMultiple(), setMultiple(), setRequired(), getDefaultValue() and setDefaultValue(); classes implementing these interfaces directly (rather than extending the provided base classes) must supply the typed-data contract too.
  • Deprecation: TypedInputsInterface::getInput()/getInputs()/setInput() and TypedOutputsInterface::getOutput()/getOutputs() are deprecated in tool:1.0.0-beta10 and removed in tool:1.0.0-rc1 (#3583019); use getInputValue()/setInputValue()/getInputData() and the output equivalents instead.
  • New API: New getInputData()/getOutputData(): TypedDataInterface methods on TypedInputsInterface/TypedOutputsInterface return typed data wrapping an input's or output's resolved value.

Technical details

TypedInputsTrait and TypedOutputsTrait used to store every value inside a core Context object purely as a value holder, calling only getContextValue(), getContextData() and validate() on it. That wrapper is now gone from storage: values are held as typed data (TypedDataManager::create()) or, for an explicit NULL, a bare marker that resolves through the definition's default the way a value-less Context used to. A new internal helper, Drupal\tool\TypedData\EffectiveDataDefinition::createFrom(), rebuilds a fresh core data definition of the declared data type (merging the author's constraints with the type's own defaults) whenever a value needs to be created, validated, or turned into a JSON Schema; it replaces the ad hoc new Context($definition, $value) calls previously scattered through validation and normalization.

getInput()/getOutput()/getInputs()/getOutputs()/setInput() remain on the interfaces but are deprecated; internally they now mint a Context on demand via mintInputContext()/mintOutputContext() rather than reading it from storage. ContextDefinitionNormalizer (used to build the advertised JSON Schema) was retargeted to work directly against InputDefinitionInterface/OutputDefinitionInterface (through getDataDefinition(), backed by EffectiveDataDefinition) while still accepting plain core ContextDefinitionInterface objects, since the ai module's setContextDefinitionOverride() path and the #3583015 acceptance shim still deliver those.

Because the ai module's function-call contract is still typed on core ContextDefinitionInterface, tool_ai_connector gained an adaptation layer at that boundary: ToolContextDefinition/ToolEntityContextDefinition (implementing a new ToolContextDefinitionInterface) wrap a Tool API definition inside a core context definition, and ToolPluginBase::getContextDefinitions()/applyContextDefinitionOverridesToInputSchema() convert back and forth so overrides made by the ai module (setContextDefinitionOverride()) still take effect. Output validation for entity values was also narrowed to only run the effective definition's EntityType/Bundle constraints (the declared-type checks), rather than the wrapped entity's own full constraint set (e.g. EntityChanged), matching the shape checking the rest of output validation already did. The core TypedDataManager prototype-cache workaround (resetTypedDataPrototypes(), worked around pending core #3616328) is retained rather than removed, and its kernel coverage was extended to cover output validation as well as inputs. Related work: #3583016 is the parent plan issue, #3583017 re-parented the definition families onto typed data, and #3583019 will remove the deprecated context accessors and the remaining ContextDefinitionInterface parentage.

Upgrade

Replace calls to the deprecated context accessors with the value or typed-data accessors:

// Before
$value = $tool->getInput('name')->getContextValue();
$tool->setInput('name', new Context($definition, $value));

// After
$value = $tool->getInputValue('name');
// or, for typed data:
$data = $tool->getInputData('name');
$tool->setInputValue('name', $value);

The same applies to outputs: replace getOutput()/setOutput()-style usage with getOutputValue()/setOutputValue()/getOutputData(). getInputs()/getOutputs() (which returned all values as Context objects) should be replaced with getInputValues()/getOutputValues(), or getInputData()/getOutputData() per name if a typed-data wrapper is needed. All deprecated methods will be removed in tool:1.0.0-rc1 (#3583019).

If you implement InputDefinitionInterface or OutputDefinitionInterface directly rather than extending the provided base classes (InputDefinition, MapInputDefinition, etc.), add implementations for isMultiple(), setMultiple(), setRequired(), getDefaultValue() and setDefaultValue(), since the interfaces now extend DataDefinitionInterface as well as ContextDefinitionInterface.

item.title: #3585934: Resource access denials return -32603 because the SDK's ReadResourceHandler swallows the exception
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3585934 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

Before this fix, when an MCP client called resources/read for a resource it wasn't allowed to access, the site answered with HTTP 200 and a generic JSON-RPC -32603 internal error saying "Error while reading resource," giving the client no indication that access was actually denied, and logging a spurious error for what is really a routine permission check. Now a denied read answers the same way a request for a nonexistent resource does: a -32002 (or -32602 on newer protocol versions) "resource not found" error. This intentionally doesn't reveal that the resource exists at all, matching how the rest of MCP handles resources a client can't see.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ResourceContentCache::generate() now throws Mcp\Exception\ResourceNotFoundException instead of Drupal\mcp_server\Exception\McpAuthorizationDeniedException for a denied resource access check, and for the same exception (previously a plain \RuntimeException) when the content callback returns NULL.

Technical details

The root cause is that the php-sdk's ReadResourceHandler catches any \Throwable it doesn't specifically recognize and converts it into a generic -32603 internal error, logging it at error level. ResourceContentCache::generate(), which both ResourceProviderHandler and ResourceTemplateProviderHandler delegate to for the access check plus cache lookup, was throwing Drupal\mcp_server\Exception\McpAuthorizationDeniedException on a denied checkAccess(), which the SDK doesn't know how to map, so it fell into that generic path.

The fix changes ResourceContentCache::generate() to throw Mcp\Exception\ResourceNotFoundException in that case instead, which the SDK does recognize and maps to a proper resource-not-found JSON-RPC error. The same exception is now also thrown when the content callback returns NULL (previously a plain \RuntimeException), so a denied read and a missing resource are indistinguishable to the client by design, avoiding disclosure that a forbidden resource exists. McpAuthorizationDeniedException itself is untouched and still used for OAuth-scope related failures elsewhere (McpServerController, McpExceptionSubscriber, Drush commands); only the resource-read path stopped using it. A new kernel test, ResourceReadErrorTest, exercises this through the actual /mcp endpoint and asserts a denied read and a missing read produce identical error payloads. ResourceProviderRegistrationTest was updated to expect ResourceNotFoundException for both the forbidden and missing cases. The SDK still logs both cases at error level; a quieter log level needs an upstream fix, tracked at https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/php-sdk/issues/513.

Upgrade

If custom code catches the exception thrown by ResourceContentCache::generate() for a denied resource read, update it:

// Before
catch (\Drupal\mcp_server\Exception\McpAuthorizationDeniedException $e) {
  // ...
}

// After
catch (\Mcp\Exception\ResourceNotFoundException $e) {
  // $e->uri holds the requested URI.
}

A NULL return from a resource plugin's content callback now also throws Mcp\Exception\ResourceNotFoundException instead of a plain \RuntimeException.

item.title: #3583034: tool:run --json prints raw output values instead of the published ones
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583034 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Running drush tool:run --json printed a different, unpublished view of a tool's output than the one MCP clients and tool:info's schema describe. For example a date-time output came out as a raw Unix timestamp integer instead of the RFC 3339 string the schema promises, and an entity output came out as its PHP class name (like Drupal\node\Entity\Node) instead of the handle string MCP actually receives. This made the --json output untrustworthy for anyone scripting against it or comparing it to the advertised schema. The fix makes tool:run --json print the same, published values every other consumer sees.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ToolRunCommand::runCommand() read $tool->getOutputValues(), the raw PHP-side view of a tool's outputs, and passed it through a hand-rolled serializeOutputs() helper that mapped objects via toArray(), __toString(), or get_class() as a fallback. That path never ran the output transform events that getFormattedResult()->getContextValues() runs, so entities never became handles and, once related timestamp/decimal/datetime formatting work landed, dated and decimal values wouldn't match their declared JSON Schema either. The fix reads $tool->getFormattedResult()->getContextValues() instead and drops serializeOutputs() entirely, since those values are already the ones destined for Json::encode(). The text-mode output path keeps using formatOutputValue() on the same, now-formatted values.

item.title: #3583041: Issue #3583041: Keep a multiple definition's description on the array
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583041 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

The Tool module builds JSON Schema descriptions of each tool's inputs, which are consumed by AI agents and MCP clients to know what a tool accepts. For inputs that accept multiple values (multiple: TRUE), the schema generator previously threw away the field's own description and title, replacing them with a generic Array of <label> string, while duplicating the real label and description onto the nested items schema instead. This meant the actual, useful description written by the tool's author was hidden one level down instead of appearing where a caller would look for it. The fix keeps the field's real title and description on the array schema itself, where they belong, and leaves items to describe only the type of each element.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: For context definitions with multiple: TRUE, ContextDefinitionNormalizer no longer duplicates the label/description onto items or rewrites the array's own description as Array of <label>; the definition's real description and title now stay directly on the array schema, and items carries only its type (and constraints like format).

The bug was in ContextDefinitionNormalizer::normalize() in the tool module: when handling a multiple context definition, the code cloned the item definition, normalized it to build items, then copied that clone's description onto items['description'] and synthesized $schema['description'] = 'Array of ' . $object->getLabel(), overwriting whatever description the array schema already had.

The fix clears the label and description on the cloned single-item definition before normalizing it ($item_definition->setLabel(''); $item_definition->setDescription('');), so items no longer picks up a redundant title/description, and removes the block that rewrote $schema['description'] to the generic Array of ... string. The array's own title and description, already set earlier in the method from the definition, are left untouched. Kernel tests in InputSchemaMatrixTest and RicherSchemaEmissionTest were updated to assert the corrected shape, e.g. a multi_string field now emits {"items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Multi string: A multiple string input.", "title": "Multi string"} instead of nesting the description inside items and replacing the top-level description with "Array of Multi string".</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Code or tests that assert on the exact JSON Schema produced for multiple tool inputs must be updated. {
  "type": ["array", "null"],
  "items": {
    "type": "string",
    "description": "Multi string: A multiple string input.",
    "title": "Multi string"
  },
  "description": "Array of Multi string",
  "title": "Multi string"
}

to:

{
  "type": ["array", "null"],
  "items": { "type": "string" },
  "description": "Multi string: A multiple string input.",

item.title: #3583029: Enforce required outputs in ToolBase::execute() so a success cannot omit a declared output
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3583029 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

The Tool API's OutputDefinition has always defaulted required to TRUE, but nothing enforced it: a tool could return ExecutableResult::success() without setting one of its own required outputs and execute() would report success anyway. A caller would only discover the problem later, either from an exception when reading the missing value or, worse, not at all if it just read the raw context values off the formatted result. Now execute() validates the outputs right after a successful doExecute() and, if a required output is missing or a set value doesn't match its declared shape, replaces the result with a failure categorized as Runtime and logs the violation against the tool. This closes the gap that had forced the MCP Server Tool Bridge module to omit required from the JSON Schema it advertises for tool outputs, since it could not promise something the Tool API itself did not guarantee.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ToolBase::execute() now fails a tool (with FailureCategory::Runtime) instead of silently succeeding when a doExecute() implementation omits a declared required output, sets it to NULL, or sets a value that violates its output definition.

Technical details

The check lives in a new private ToolBase::failOnOutputViolations(), called from execute() immediately after the loop that copies matching context values into $this->outputs. It calls the existing validateOutputs() and, if the returned ConstraintViolationList is non-empty, logs the violation against the tool's plugin ID and overwrites $this->result with ExecutableResult::failure(..., FailureCategory::Runtime), since a missing or malformed output is a bug in the tool, not something the caller can fix by changing its arguments.

TypedOutputsTrait::validateOutputs() was rewritten to check shape as well as presence: an output whose Context::hasContextValue() is false now counts as unset (previously only a wholly-absent key did, so a required output explicitly set to NULL slipped through), and each set value is run through a new private validateOutputValue() that mirrors TypedInputsTrait::validateInputValue(). Multiple-value and ListOutputDefinition outputs are checked item by item with the failing index named in the message; MapOutputDefinition properties are checked individually, with missing required properties reported by name; and entity-typed outputs (data type entity or entity:*) are only checked for being an EntityInterface instance, not run through full entity field validation, so a tool that merely returns an entity it loaded is not failed for that entity's own data problems. The item/property-naming helper and the core TypedDataManager prototype-cache workaround (for the upstream bug in drupal/drupal#3616328) were extracted from TypedInputsTrait into a new shared ValueViolationsTrait, used by both input and output validation.

Test coverage was added via two new fixture plugins, RequiredOutputTool and EntityOutputTool, plus tests/src/Kernel/Tool/OutputValidationTest.php and additions to ToolBaseTest, covering a missing or NULL required output failing with the output named, an omitted optional output still succeeding, an invalid output value failing the same way, and entity outputs being validated by shape rather than by full field validation.

Upgrade

Any tool plugin whose doExecute() can return a success without setting a value for one of its declared output_definitions will now fail instead. For each such output, either always set it:

protected function doExecute(array $values): ExecutableResult {
  // Make sure every required output is set on every success path.
  return ExecutableResult::success($message, ['answer' => $computed_value]);
}

or mark it optional in the plugin's output_definitions if it legitimately may not always have a value:

output_definitions: [
  'link' => new OutputDefinition(
    data_type: 'uri',
    label: new TranslatableMarkup('Link'),
    description: new TranslatableMarkup('An optional uri output.'),
    required: FALSE,
  ),
],

A kernel test (OutputSchemaTest) covers both the normal case, asserting required only lists outputs marked required, and the no-output case, asserting the empty properties bag encodes as {}.

item.title: #3582991: Drush tool:run should surface access denial reason and pre-flight validation
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3582991 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The tool:run Drush command now tells you why it refused to run a tool instead of a generic "Access denied" message. It validates the tool's inputs first, so a bad or missing argument is reported as an input problem rather than a permission problem, and when access truly is denied, it surfaces the actual reason the tool gave (for example, which permission is missing). With --json, every pre-execution failure now also includes a machine-readable error_type field, useful for scripts, CI pipelines, or AI agents driving Drush programmatically.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The tool:run Drush command's --json error output gains a new error_type field (backed by the RunErrorType enum), and now validates tool inputs before checking access rather than after.

Technical details

ToolRunCommand::run() in the tool module now calls $tool->validateInputs() before checking access, since access() fails closed with a generic reason on invalid input; checking access first would misreport a bad argument as a permission problem. If violations exist, the command reports them and exits before ever calling access().

The access check itself now calls $tool->access(return_as_object: TRUE) and, when the result implements AccessResultReasonInterface, appends getReason() to the error message instead of dropping it.

Every failure path in the command now passes a new RunErrorType backed enum (src/Drush/RunErrorType.php) to writeError(), which serializes it as error_type in the --json output: tool_not_found, invalid_option, user_not_found, user_blocked, invalid_input, access_denied, and execution_failed. A tool that runs and reports its own failure (a failed ExecutableResult) is not one of these: it has no error_type, since that's a result, not a command error. The docs at docs/usage/drush.md document the ordering, the JSON shape, and each error type. A new test fixture, InvalidOutputTool, exercises the one execution failure ToolBase doesn't absorb: a result whose output value doesn't fit its output definition, which makes execute() itself throw after doExecute() already succeeded.

Upgrade

Scripts or CI pipelines invoking drush tool:run --json and inspecting failures should switch from string-matching the error message to reading the new error_type field:

{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Access denied for tool 'send_email': The 'send emails' permission is required.",
  "error_type": "access_denied"
}

Possible error_type values: tool_not_found, invalid_option, user_not_found, user_blocked, invalid_input, access_denied, execution_failed. Note that a tool which runs and reports its own failure has no error_type at all, that document is a result (success: false plus the tool's own message), not a command error.
